<section id="quality" aria-labelledby="quality-heading">
<div class="section-heading"><span class="section-number" aria-hidden="true">03</span><div><p class="eyebrow">BEFORE INTERPRETING RESULTS</p><h2 id="quality-heading">Time and location quality</h2></div></div>
<div class="quality-block"><h3>Timestamp reliability</h3>
<p>Timestamp diagnostics are screening rules, not proof that times are accurate. Darkness analysis excludes force-months that fail or lack a reliable-time flag.</p>

{{timestamps}}

</div>
<div class="quality-block"><h3>Location and boundary sensitivity</h3>
<p>Coordinates are anonymised snap points. Boundary sensitivity measures proximity to a geography edge; it does not measure or correct true location error. The boundary-sensitive share uses assigned events with measured distances. Missing-coordinate and unassigned shares use all supplied events.</p>

{{geography}}

</div>

<section id="estimates" aria-labelledby="estimates-heading">
<div class="section-heading"><span class="section-number" aria-hidden="true">04</span><div><p class="eyebrow">RESULTS WITH CONTEXT</p><h2 id="estimates-heading">Estimates</h2></div></div>
<p>Each supplied analysis retains its own scope, exposures and exclusions. Rates use submitted population-time. Consult the scope details beneath each result before comparing analyses.</p>
<div class="uncertainty-guide">
<div><span class="guide-label">SAMPLING UNCERTAINTY</span><p>Intervals condition on the model and denominator. They do not cover missing ethnicity, population movement, Census measurement or incomplete submissions.</p></div>
<div><span class="guide-label">ASSUMPTION RANGE</span><p>Sensitivity ranges describe stated scenarios. They are reported separately and are not confidence intervals.</p></div>
</div>

<section id="interpretation" aria-labelledby="interpretation-heading">
<div class="section-heading"><span class="section-number" aria-hidden="true">05</span><div><p class="eyebrow">HOW TO READ THE EVIDENCE</p><h2 id="interpretation-heading">Assumptions and limitations</h2></div></div>
<div class="interpretation-card"><h3>Assumptions</h3>
<p>Resident Census population is an exposure choice. It may differ from the people present or exposed to police activity. Missing-ethnicity allocations are stated scenarios. Their ranges are not confidence intervals and are not combined with sampling uncertainty. Spatial smoothing stabilises under its model assumptions; inspect unsmoothed data, local changes and convergence diagnostics.</p>
<h4>Statements supplied for this report</h4>

{{assumptions}}

</div>
<div class="interpretation-card"><h3>Limitations</h3>
<p>Repeated events, deployment, activity, selection and measurement can affect comparisons. Hit rates condition on being searched and do not by themselves establish discrimination. Darkness associations require assumptions about visibility and comparable activity and deployment. The method originated for vehicle stops; its transfer to pedestrian searches requires justification. Neither an undefined result nor a wide interval establishes absence of disparity.</p>
<h4>Statements supplied for this report</h4>

{{limitations}}

</div>
